doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: How she would approach a commission
summary: Asked what she would ask a commissioner, she says she would learn about the person's place and culture, like a painting commission.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Wow. Well I’d like to talk about your extensive range of compositions. Can you describe where — let’s suppose I commissioned you for something for Hamilton College, something new.
What would be the first question you would ask of me for some guidelines.

I think, whoa that’s a big one. I’m certainly not going to dump my world onto yours and go I’m just going to do this. I would want to get to know a little bit about the space you’re living in and what is feeding your environment culturally and through the natural and through the urban environment and what is — even historically. Maybe there’s some great figure there that I want to put a lens on. Do you know what I mean? I like to put my lens on things. Or, a lens on your — things that are important to you, and try to capture that I suppose through my music. I would also want to know what level of musicians I’m writing for too, although that’s basically it. I’d want to have a conversation. I’d want to go for lunch and go, “Tell me about yourself. You’re going to commission me? I want to know why this interests you and what is the feeling in the music that you want to have.

It’s kind of like a painting. It’s like if you commission me for a painting you’re going to give me a subject matter, most likely, unless you’re like no I don’t want that, it’s like all about Christine and whatever space she’s in she can just write whatever she wants. Or we approach it another way which is like tell me — I want to get to know what elements I’m dealing with from your space.

That’s very illuminating I think. Because some people might say well I want to know the instrumentation and what are you going to pay me, really logistical things, but it makes sense with what I’ve been reading about you. And what if I said, “Okay I want another ‘Habitat’ from you.” Habitat part two.
